items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: And what Ike had showed me, the licks, I put a few of them in, they gave me a couple of breaks, and gave me a couple of intros.

ctx.x: he was fat, looking fat and sassy. Well, the man, sure, Jim, he'd play around a little bit. And Mitchell has often said that he didn't know what he was doing in the jazz field, because he'd started out as a classical musician, and he just kind of figured he always was a classical musician. But he had to sell his horn, and the best way to do it was to play a little jazz. Did you stay with Wickliffe when they went on the stage with Dave and Tressie? Dave and Tressie, yes. You did?

I was with Wickliffe and Tressie and Ike, they got a picture they're gonna give me of who I looked when I was young. And I will. You two fellas been together a long time then. Oh, I know Nike. Well, I tell you, when the times started changing and the banjos got so popular, I went and got a banjo. And by knowing harmony and I knew the piano pretty good, and I stayed home for four solid months with that banjo. And so a fellow told me, says, you play good, but you're playing too straight. He says, why don't you go…
to make it to New York. What year was that? I forget the year.
